issue.title: Bead update, claim, remove, and ready-mark events record the bead creator as actor instead of the acting agent
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1rg.10 (epic sase-1rg, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1); triaged by the
sase-1rg land agent on 2026-11-06. The epic plan anticipated this and deliberately kept it
out of the open-actor phase.

sase-1rg.10 fixed `run_open` in sase-core so `IssueOpened` records the acting opener
(`open_issue_with_actor`, `Option<String>` actor, store-owner fallback like close) instead
of `issue.created_by`. The same creator-as-actor pattern remains in every other mutation
listed below, so bead history blames the bead's creator (for phase beads, the epic's
creating session) for writes made by a different agent or human.

Call sites in sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation/` that pass
`&issue.created_by` (or `&ancestor.created_by`) as the `stage_event` actor:

- `notes_update.rs` `run_update`: the `IssueUpdated` event, plus the ancestor
  `IssueOpened` events from reopening closed ancestors.
- `claims.rs`: `run_claim_launch`, `run_claim_wait`, `run_claim_release`, and
  `run_preclaim` (`EpicWorkPreclaimed`).
- `close_remove.rs`: the `IssueRemoved` event in `remove_issues` / `remove_issue`.
- `store.rs`: the `ReadyMarked` / `ReadyUnmarked` event.

Fix: follow the sase-1rg.10 template (sase-core commit 28159925, sase commit a6fe55c1be).
Add an optional actor to each mutation, falling back to the store owner. Thread it
through the PyO3 bindings and the Python facades/CLI handlers (`resolve_mutation_author`).
Add Rust tests modelled on `mutation/tests/open.rs` and `mutation/tests/close.rs`, plus
Python tests. Move `sase-core-revision.txt` past the sase-core commit per
`docs/rust_backend.md`. For claims, decide deliberately whether the actor is the runner
(host) or the launched agent. The launched agent is already recorded in the payload.

task_type_fields.impact: Bead event history and anything built on it (audits, `sase bead history`, health watches attributing demotions or claims to sessions) blame the bead creator, usually the epic-creating session for phase beads, instead of the real actor. No data loss, but it misleads investigations such as the sase-1rg F6 demotion analysis.
task_type_fields.repro: In a test store, create a bead as owner A, then run `sase bead update <id> --title X` (or `sase bead rm`, or a claim/release through the runner) as agent B. `sase bead history <id> --format full` records actor A, not B, on the IssueUpdated / IssueRemoved / claim events. In code: `grep -n 'created_by' crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation/{notes_update,claims,close_remove,store}.rs` in sase-core shows each `stage_event` actor argument.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1rg fixed the creator-as-actor bug only for bead open; update, claims, remove, and ready-mark events still attribute writes to the bead's creator, so bead history misattributes who changed a bead.
